title: Computer Programming II
source_note: Standard NUC-aligned second-course programming curriculum (functions, arrays, pointers, structures, recursion, file handling, and an introduction to object-oriented concepts), grounded in LASU's CSC218 'Foundation of Sequential Program' and CSC226 'Object Oriented Programming I (C++)' course descriptions as the natural continuation after an introductory programming course.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of using functions (or procedures) in a program?
options: They allow code reuse and break a program into manageable, modular units
They make a program run only once
They automatically fix all logic errors
They remove the need for variables
questions.correct_answer: They allow code reuse and break a program into manageable, modular units
questions.explanation: Functions enable modular programming by allowing a block of code to be written once and reused multiple times, improving readability and maintainability.

questions.question: In programming, what is the difference between 'pass by value' and 'pass by reference' when calling a function?
options: Pass by value copies the argument's data, while pass by reference gives the function direct access to the original variable
Pass by value and pass by reference always behave identically
Pass by reference only works with numeric data types
Pass by value permanently deletes the original variable
questions.correct_answer: Pass by value copies the argument's data, while pass by reference gives the function direct access to the original variable
questions.explanation: Pass by value sends a copy of the argument's data to the function, so changes inside the function do not affect the original; pass by reference allows the function to modify the original variable.

questions.question: What is recursion in programming?
options: A technique where a function calls itself to solve a smaller instance of the same problem
A method of sorting an array in reverse order
A type of syntax error
A way to permanently store data on disk
questions.correct_answer: A technique where a function calls itself to solve a smaller instance of the same problem
questions.explanation: Recursion occurs when a function invokes itself, typically to break a problem into smaller sub-problems, until it reaches a base case that stops the recursive calls.

questions.question: Every correctly written recursive function must have which essential component to avoid infinite recursion?
options: A base case that terminates the recursive calls
A global variable
A loop statement
A pointer variable
questions.correct_answer: A base case that terminates the recursive calls
questions.explanation: A base case provides a condition under which the function stops calling itself, preventing infinite recursion and eventual stack overflow.

questions.question: An array is best described as:
options: A collection of elements of the same data type stored in contiguous memory locations
A single variable that can hold only one value
A function that returns multiple data types
A file used to store program output
questions.correct_answer: A collection of elements of the same data type stored in contiguous memory locations
questions.explanation: An array is a data structure that stores a fixed-size, ordered collection of elements of the same type, contiguous in memory, accessed via an index.

questions.question: In most programming languages, what is the index of the first element in an array?
options: It depends only on the array's data type
questions.explanation: Most programming languages (such as C, C++, and Java) use zero-based indexing, meaning the first element of an array is accessed with index 0.

questions.question: What is a two-dimensional array typically used to represent?
options: Data arranged in rows and columns, such as a matrix or table
A single list of numbers only
A function with two parameters
A file with two lines of text
questions.correct_answer: Data arranged in rows and columns, such as a matrix or table
questions.explanation: A two-dimensional array organizes data in a grid-like structure with rows and columns, making it suitable for representing matrices, tables, and grids.

questions.question: A pointer variable in languages like C/C++ is used to:
options: Store the memory address of another variable
Store only text strings
Automatically sort an array
Replace the need for functions
questions.correct_answer: Store the memory address of another variable
questions.explanation: A pointer is a variable that holds the memory address of another variable, allowing indirect access to and manipulation of that variable's data.

questions.question: In C, what does the dereference operator (*) do when applied to a pointer?
options: It accesses the value stored at the memory address the pointer refers to
It converts the pointer into an integer permanently
It deletes the pointer from memory
It multiplies the pointer's address by two
questions.correct_answer: It accesses the value stored at the memory address the pointer refers to
questions.explanation: The dereference operator (*) retrieves or sets the value at the memory location that a pointer is pointing to.

questions.question: What is 'dynamic memory allocation'?
options: Allocating memory for variables at runtime rather than at compile time
Allocating memory only when the computer is first powered on
A technique that removes the need for the operating system
A way to permanently prevent memory from being freed
questions.correct_answer: Allocating memory for variables at runtime rather than at compile time
questions.explanation: Dynamic memory allocation allows a program to request and release memory while it is running, offering flexibility that static, compile-time allocation does not provide.

questions.question: In C, which function is commonly used to dynamically allocate memory on the heap?
options: malloc()
printf()
scanf()
main()
questions.correct_answer: malloc()
questions.explanation: The malloc() function in C dynamically allocates a specified number of bytes on the heap and returns a pointer to the allocated memory block.

questions.question: What can happen if dynamically allocated memory is not freed after use?
options: A memory leak, where unused memory remains reserved and unavailable for reuse
The program automatically runs faster
The compiler will refuse to compile the program
The operating system will immediately crash
questions.correct_answer: A memory leak, where unused memory remains reserved and unavailable for reuse
questions.explanation: Failing to free dynamically allocated memory causes a memory leak, where that memory remains reserved but inaccessible, potentially exhausting available memory over time.

questions.question: A structure (struct) in programming is used to:
options: Group related variables of different data types under a single name
Store only a single integer value
Automatically generate a graphical user interface
Compile source code into machine language
questions.correct_answer: Group related variables of different data types under a single name
questions.explanation: A struct is a user-defined data type that groups variables of possibly different types together under one name, useful for representing composite records.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes file handling in programming?
options: The process of creating, reading, writing, and closing files from within a program
The process of designing a computer's physical case
The process of compiling source code
The process of installing an operating system
questions.correct_answer: The process of creating, reading, writing, and closing files from within a program
questions.explanation: File handling refers to the operations a program performs to interact with files, including opening, reading data from, writing data to, and closing them.

questions.question: Why is it important to close a file after a program finishes using it?
options: To ensure all buffered data is written to disk and system resources are released
To permanently delete the file
To convert the file into an executable program
To prevent the file from ever being opened again
questions.correct_answer: To ensure all buffered data is written to disk and system resources are released
questions.explanation: Closing a file flushes any buffered output to disk and releases the file handle/resources back to the operating system, preventing data loss or resource leaks.

questions.question: What distinguishes a text file from a binary file?
options: A text file stores human-readable characters, while a binary file stores data in a non-human-readable, raw format
A binary file can only store the numbers 0 and 1 as separate characters
A text file cannot be opened by any program
There is no real difference between the two
questions.correct_answer: A text file stores human-readable characters, while a binary file stores data in a non-human-readable, raw format
questions.explanation: Text files store data as readable characters (like ASCII), while binary files store data in a raw, often non-readable format that closely mirrors how data is represented in memory.

questions.question: What is 'encapsulation' in object-oriented programming?
options: Bundling data and the methods that operate on that data within a single unit (class), often restricting direct access to some components
The process of compiling a program into machine code
A technique for connecting to the internet
The process of deleting unused classes
questions.correct_answer: Bundling data and the methods that operate on that data within a single unit (class), often restricting direct access to some components
questions.explanation: Encapsulation combines data and the functions that operate on it into a single class, while restricting direct external access to some of the object's internal details.

questions.question: In object-oriented programming, what is a 'class'?
options: A blueprint or template that defines the properties and behaviors of objects
A single instance of a running program
A type of loop structure
A file extension for compiled code
questions.correct_answer: A blueprint or template that defines the properties and behaviors of objects
questions.explanation: A class is a template that defines the attributes (data) and methods (behavior) that its instances (objects) will have.

questions.question: What is the relationship between a class and an object?
options: An object is an instance of a class
A class is an instance of an object
Classes and objects are unrelated concepts
A class can only exist after all objects are deleted
questions.correct_answer: An object is an instance of a class
questions.explanation: An object is a concrete instantiation of a class, created using the structure and behavior defined by that class.

questions.question: What programming concept allows a subclass to acquire properties and behaviors from a parent class?
options: Inheritance
Encapsulation
Recursion
Iteration
questions.correct_answer: Inheritance
questions.explanation: Inheritance allows a new class (subclass) to reuse, extend, or modify the behavior defined in another class (superclass), promoting code reuse.

questions.question: What does 'polymorphism' allow in object-oriented programming?
options: Objects of different classes to be treated through a common interface, often responding differently to the same method call
A program to run without ever being compiled
Variables to change their data type permanently at runtime only once
Files to be automatically encrypted
questions.correct_answer: Objects of different classes to be treated through a common interface, often responding differently to the same method call
questions.explanation: Polymorphism allows objects of different classes to be accessed through a common interface, with each class providing its own specific implementation of shared methods.

questions.question: What is 'data abstraction' in programming?
options: Hiding complex implementation details and exposing only the essential features of an object
Converting analog data into digital data
Deleting all comments from source code
Storing data permanently on a hard disk
questions.correct_answer: Hiding complex implementation details and exposing only the essential features of an object
questions.explanation: Data abstraction focuses on exposing only the necessary, relevant details of an object to the user while hiding the internal implementation complexity.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a linked list compared to an array?
options: A linked list allows dynamic growth and efficient insertion/deletion without shifting elements, unlike a fixed-size array
A linked list must always be a fixed size like an array
A linked list can only store one element at a time
A linked list is always faster to search than an array
questions.correct_answer: A linked list allows dynamic growth and efficient insertion/deletion without shifting elements, unlike a fixed-size array
questions.explanation: Linked lists use nodes connected by pointers, allowing dynamic resizing and efficient insertions/deletions, whereas arrays have fixed sizes and require shifting elements for insertion/deletion.
questions.topic: Introduction to data structures in programming

questions.question: What is a string in most high-level programming languages?
options: A sequence of characters typically used to represent text
A single numeric digit
A type of loop construct
A memory address pointing to hardware
questions.correct_answer: A sequence of characters typically used to represent text
questions.explanation: A string is a data type representing a sequence of characters, commonly used to store and manipulate textual data in programs.

questions.question: Which built-in operation is commonly used to join two or more strings together?
options: Concatenation
Differentiation
Normalization
Compilation
questions.correct_answer: Concatenation
questions.explanation: Concatenation is the operation of joining two or more strings end-to-end to form a single combined string.

questions.question: What is the purpose of exception handling (e.g. try-catch blocks) in a program?
options: To detect and gracefully handle runtime errors without abruptly crashing the program
To speed up compilation time
To automatically translate code between programming languages
To permanently disable all error messages
questions.correct_answer: To detect and gracefully handle runtime errors without abruptly crashing the program
questions.explanation: Exception handling mechanisms allow a program to detect runtime errors (exceptions) and respond to them gracefully, rather than terminating unexpectedly.

questions.question: What is the difference between a compile-time error and a runtime error?
options: A compile-time error is detected before the program runs, while a runtime error occurs while the program is executing
A runtime error always prevents the program from compiling
A compile-time error only occurs in interpreted languages
There is no difference between them
questions.correct_answer: A compile-time error is detected before the program runs, while a runtime error occurs while the program is executing
questions.explanation: Compile-time errors (e.g. syntax errors) are caught by the compiler before execution, while runtime errors (e.g. division by zero) occur while the program is running.

questions.question: What does 'modular programming' emphasize?
options: Dividing a program into separate, independent modules or functions that each handle a specific task
Writing an entire program as a single continuous block of code with no functions
Avoiding the use of variables entirely
Using only global variables throughout the program
questions.correct_answer: Dividing a program into separate, independent modules or functions that each handle a specific task
questions.explanation: Modular programming breaks a program into smaller, self-contained modules (functions or units), improving organization, reusability, and maintainability.

questions.question: What is a 'local variable' in the context of function scope?
options: A variable declared inside a function that is only accessible within that function
A variable that can be accessed from any part of the program
A variable stored permanently on a hard disk
A variable that never changes its value
questions.correct_answer: A variable declared inside a function that is only accessible within that function
questions.explanation: A local variable is declared within a function or block and exists only within that scope, becoming inaccessible once the function finishes executing.

questions.question: What is a 'global variable'?
options: A variable declared outside all functions, accessible from anywhere in the program
A variable that only exists inside one specific loop
A variable that automatically deletes itself after one use
A variable that can only store Boolean values
questions.correct_answer: A variable declared outside all functions, accessible from anywhere in the program
questions.explanation: A global variable is declared outside of any function, giving it program-wide scope so it can be accessed and modified from any part of the code.

questions.question: In sorting an array of numbers using a simple exchange-based algorithm, what is the primary operation repeated in bubble sort?
options: Comparing adjacent elements and swapping them if they are in the wrong order
Dividing the array in half recursively
Selecting a random pivot element
Hashing each element to a bucket
questions.correct_answer: Comparing adjacent elements and swapping them if they are in the wrong order
questions.explanation: Bubble sort repeatedly steps through the array, comparing each pair of adjacent elements and swapping them if they are out of order, until the array is sorted.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a linear search algorithm?
options: To sequentially check each element of a list until the target value is found or the list ends
To sort a list in ascending order only
To divide a sorted list in half repeatedly
To permanently delete elements from a list
questions.correct_answer: To sequentially check each element of a list until the target value is found or the list ends
questions.explanation: Linear search checks each element of a list one by one, in order, until it finds the target value or reaches the end of the list.
